name: Bouldering
shortDescription: Climb short, challenging routes without ropes over safety mats.
hook: It's a physical puzzle where your body is the key.

experiment.smallestStep: Rent shoes and climb V0s (the easiest routes) until your forearms give out.
experiment.whatSuccessFeelsLike: Your arms are pumped, but you finally figured out how to shift your hips to reach the top hold.
experiment.commonBeginnerMistake: Using only arms to pull up instead of pushing with legs.
experiment.nextStep: Go twice a week for a month to build tendon strength.

surprisingAdjacencies.explanation: Both require looking ahead and mapping a sequence of moves before executing.
Finding the right hold position is like feeling for the binding pin.

name: Wheel Throwing
shortDescription: Shape clay on a spinning wheel into bowls, cups, and vessels.
hook: The clay fights back, and winning feels incredible.

experiment.smallestStep: Book a single beginner wheel-throwing class at a local pottery studio. Pay attention to how the process feels.
experiment.whatSuccessFeelsLike: You lose track of time and think about the clay the next day.
experiment.commonBeginnerMistake: Judging the output instead of paying attention to the process.
experiment.nextStep: Sign up for a 4-week beginner series.

surprisingAdjacencies.explanation: Both involve working with unpredictable material.

name: Lockpicking (Locksport)
shortDescription: Exploit mechanical vulnerabilities to open locks without the original key.
hook: Feel the invisible click of bypassing a physical security system.

practicalConstraints.equipmentNeeded: Basic pick set, clear practice lock

experiment.smallestStep: Buy a $20 starter kit with a transparent padlock and pick it while watching TV.
experiment.whatSuccessFeelsLike: The cylinder suddenly gives way and turns. It's an instant dopamine hit.
experiment.nextStep: Buy a standard Master Lock No. 3 and pick it blind.

surprisingAdjacencies.explanation: You are feeling your way through an unseen puzzle.

name: Sourdough Baking
shortDescription: Bake bread using wild yeast and long fermentation.
hook: You are literally keeping a microbial pet alive to make delicious bread.

experiment.smallestStep: Create a sourdough starter from just flour and water and feed it for 7 days.
experiment.whatSuccessFeelsLike: Seeing bubbles and smelling that distinct tangy aroma.
experiment.commonBeginnerMistake: Worrying too much about exact temperatures instead of observing the dough.
experiment.nextStep: Bake your first crusty boule.

surprisingAdjacencies.explanation: Both require balancing a delicate biological system.

name: Miniature Painting
shortDescription: Paint highly detailed small-scale figures.
hook: Bring tiny grey plastic heroes and monsters to vibrant life.

experiment.smallestStep: Buy a beginner paint set with 3 space marines and follow a 15-minute YouTube tutorial.
experiment.whatSuccessFeelsLike: Applying a 'wash' and watching all the details suddenly pop out like magic.
experiment.commonBeginnerMistake: Not thinning your paints with water.
experiment.nextStep: Learn drybrushing and edge highlighting.

surprisingAdjacencies.explanation: Fine motor skills and focus on minute details.

name: Birdwatching
shortDescription: Identify and observe wild birds in their natural habitats.
hook: Turn your neighborhood into a real-life Pokémon Snap.

practicalConstraints.equipmentNeeded: Binoculars (optional initially), Merlin Bird ID app

experiment.smallestStep: Download the Merlin Bird ID app, sit in a park for 20 minutes, and use Sound ID to identify 3 birds.
experiment.whatSuccessFeelsLike: Realizing you can name the invisible singers in the trees.
experiment.commonBeginnerMistake: Trying to see the birds before listening for them.
experiment.nextStep: Buy decent binoculars and visit a local nature reserve.

surprisingAdjacencies.explanation: Both involve tuning into signals in the noise to discover distant entities.

name: Speedcubing
shortDescription: Solve a Rubik's cube as fast as humanly possible.
hook: Master algorithmic thinking to bend a colorful cube to your will in seconds.

experiment.smallestStep: Buy a $10 magnetic cube and learn the 'white cross' stage via J Perm on YouTube.
experiment.whatSuccessFeelsLike: Solving the whole cube for the first time without looking at the cheat sheet.
experiment.commonBeginnerMistake: Trying to memorize moves visually instead of understanding how pieces move.
experiment.nextStep: Learn full CFOP method.

surprisingAdjacencies.explanation: Applying specific algorithms to solve state problems efficiently.

name: Improv Comedy
shortDescription: Create unscripted scenes and characters on the spot with a group.
hook: Learn to trust your brain and embrace failure in real time.

experiment.smallestStep: Attend a single beginner drop-in workshop. Commit to just saying 'Yes, and...' to whatever happens.
experiment.whatSuccessFeelsLike: Realizing you don't have to be funny, just honest and responsive.
experiment.commonBeginnerMistake: Trying to tell jokes instead of playing the reality of the scene.
experiment.nextStep: Enroll in Improv 101.

surprisingAdjacencies.explanation: Testing how people react to unexpected situations and rules.

name: Bookbinding
shortDescription: Sew and glue paper into beautiful, durable handmade books.
hook: Build the physical vessel for stories, using centuries-old techniques.

experiment.smallestStep: Follow a Sea Lemon tutorial to make a simple saddle-stitch notebook using printer paper.
experiment.whatSuccessFeelsLike: Holding a tight, flush spine that you stitched yourself.
experiment.commonBeginnerMistake: Not aligning the paper grain direction.
experiment.nextStep: Attempt a Coptic stitch journal with exposed spine.

surprisingAdjacencies.explanation: Similar respect for material properties and precision joinery.

name: Urban Sketching
shortDescription: Draw on location, capturing the world as you see it.
hook: Force yourself to actually look at the buildings and people you walk past every day.

experiment.smallestStep: Take a pen and notebook to a coffee shop and draw the counter for 15 minutes. No erasing.
experiment.whatSuccessFeelsLike: Entering a flow state and noticing architectural details you never saw before.
experiment.commonBeginnerMistake: Worrying about perfect perspective instead of capturing the vibe.
experiment.nextStep: Add a portable watercolor palette.

surprisingAdjacencies.explanation: Both require sitting still and deeply observing your environment.

name: Aquascaping
shortDescription: Arrange aquatic plants, rocks, and wood in an aesthetically pleasing aquarium.
hook: Paint a living underwater landscape that evolves over months.

experiment.smallestStep: Set up a 2-gallon planted jar (no fish, no filter) with cheap cuttings from a local fish store.
experiment.whatSuccessFeelsLike: Seeing the plants pearl (produce oxygen bubbles) under the light.
experiment.commonBeginnerMistake: Buying fish before the nitrogen cycle is established.
experiment.nextStep: Design a 10-gallon high-tech tank with CO2 injection.

surprisingAdjacencies.explanation: Both involve sculpting nature over long periods of time.

name: Mechanical Keyboard Building
shortDescription: Assemble, lube, and tune custom keyboards for perfect sound and feel.
hook: Turn the tool you use for 8 hours a day into a personalized acoustic masterpiece.

experiment.smallestStep: Buy a cheap hot-swappable keyboard and switch out a few keys to try different tactile feels.
experiment.whatSuccessFeelsLike: The deep, satisfying 'thock' sound when you hit the spacebar.
experiment.commonBeginnerMistake: Over-lubing the switches so they feel mushy.
experiment.nextStep: Build a custom board from scratch.

surprisingAdjacencies.explanation: Both involve extreme attention to the tactile and acoustic properties of small mechanisms.

name: Foraging
shortDescription: Identify and gather wild edible plants and mushrooms.
hook: The forest is a grocery store once you learn how to read it.

experiment.smallestStep: Walk a local trail to identify 3 common, easily recognizable wild edibles (like dandelions or wild garlic) without eating them.
experiment.whatSuccessFeelsLike: Spotting a patch of chanterelles hidden under the leaf litter.
experiment.commonBeginnerMistake: Eating something you are only 90% sure about.
experiment.nextStep: Join a local foraging walk led by an expert.

surprisingAdjacencies.explanation: Searching a landscape for hidden value.

name: Fencing
shortDescription: Compete in a fast-paced combat sport using bladed weapons.
hook: Physical chess at 100 miles per hour.

experiment.smallestStep: Take a 4-week intro class at a local club where gear is provided.
experiment.whatSuccessFeelsLike: Landing your first riposte by predicting your opponent's attack.
experiment.commonBeginnerMistake: Using only your arm instead of footwork to close distance.
experiment.nextStep: Buy your own mask and glove and start open bouting.

surprisingAdjacencies.explanation: Setting up traps and reading the opponent's intentions.

name: Ham Radio
shortDescription: Operate amateur radio equipment to communicate globally.
hook: Bounce radio waves off the ionosphere to talk to someone across the ocean.

experiment.smallestStep: Buy a $30 Baofeng radio and listen to local repeater traffic (no license needed to listen).
experiment.whatSuccessFeelsLike: Hearing a crackling voice from 500 miles away come through your handheld.
experiment.nextStep: Study for and pass the Technician class license exam.

surprisingAdjacencies.explanation: Both involve waiting patiently to observe rare or distant targets and logging them.

name: Calligraphy
shortDescription: The art of beautiful and expressive handwriting.
hook: Turn simple words into visual poetry through the mastery of the pen.

experiment.smallestStep: Buy a pilot parallel pen and trace a gothic alphabet worksheet for 30 minutes.
experiment.whatSuccessFeelsLike: The satisfying scratch of the nib and the perfect swell of a curved line.
experiment.commonBeginnerMistake: Holding the pen too tightly and cramping up.
experiment.nextStep: Learn copperplate script with a pointed nib.

surprisingAdjacencies.explanation: Both rely heavily on drilling specific angles and precise muscle memory.

name: FPV Drones
shortDescription: Build and fly high-speed racing drones using virtual reality goggles.
hook: Experience out-of-body flight at 80mph.

experiment.smallestStep: Buy a radio controller ($50) and practice in a PC simulator like Liftoff for 5 hours.
experiment.whatSuccessFeelsLike: Finally hitting a gap without crashing the virtual drone.
experiment.commonBeginnerMistake: Buying a real drone before practicing in the simulator.
experiment.nextStep: Buy a tiny whoop (micro drone) and fly it around your house.

surprisingAdjacencies.explanation: Both involve tinkering with electronics to achieve a specific performance feel.

name: Woodworking
shortDescription: Cut, shape, and join wood to create furniture or art.
hook: Turn raw timber into functional heirlooms with your own hands.

experiment.smallestStep: Take a 1-day intro class at a makerspace to build a simple cutting board.
experiment.whatSuccessFeelsLike: The smell of sawdust and applying the final coat of oil.
experiment.commonBeginnerMistake: Ignoring the grain direction when planing or routing.
experiment.nextStep: Buy a Japanese pull saw and practice cutting straight lines.

surprisingAdjacencies.explanation: Both require understanding how organic materials react to environment and time.

name: Board Game Design
shortDescription: Create mechanics, rules, and prototypes for tabletop games.
hook: Engineer fun by designing systems that people play.

experiment.smallestStep: Take a game you love, change one core rule, and playtest it with a friend.
experiment.whatSuccessFeelsLike: Watching your friends get excited and argue over the rules you created.
experiment.commonBeginnerMistake: Focusing on art before the core loop is fun.
experiment.nextStep: Create a paper prototype of an original mechanic.

surprisingAdjacencies.explanation: Both rely on understanding and guiding human interaction in real time.

name: Letterpress Printing
shortDescription: Arrange lead type and press it into paper to create tactile prints.
hook: Experience the heavy, industrial origins of graphic design.

experiment.smallestStep: Book a workshop at a local printmaking studio to set your name in type.
experiment.whatSuccessFeelsLike: Pulling the lever and feeling the deep impression in the thick cotton paper.
experiment.commonBeginnerMistake: Spelling words backwards when setting the type.
experiment.nextStep: Take a multi-week course to learn registration and multi-color prints.

surprisingAdjacencies.explanation: Both obsess over the mechanical interaction between machine and text.

name: Geocaching
shortDescription: Dive deep into the world of Geocaching and master its unique challenges.
hook: Discover why people become obsessed with Geocaching.

experiment.smallestStep: Spend one weekend afternoon watching a tutorial on Geocaching and doing the absolute basics.
experiment.whatSuccessFeelsLike: Losing track of time while trying to figure it out.
experiment.nextStep: Join a dedicated community forum or local group.

surprisingAdjacencies.explanation: Both reward consistent, methodical effort.
Both involve figuring out a pathway to a goal.

experiment.smallestStep: Spend one weekend afternoon watching a tutorial on Vermicomposting and doing the absolute basics.
experiment.whatSuccessFeelsLike: Losing track of time while trying to figure it out.
experiment.nextStep: Join a dedicated community forum or local group.

surprisingAdjacencies.explanation: Both reward consistent, methodical effort.
Both involve figuring out a pathway to a goal.

name: Underground Clubbing
shortDescription: Immerse yourself in heavy electronic music and dancing in a dark, high-energy environment.
hook: Lose yourself in the rhythm and anonymous collective energy of a crowd.

experiment.smallestStep: Find a local electronic music venue on Resident Advisor and buy a ticket for this Friday.
experiment.whatSuccessFeelsLike: Feeling the bass in your chest and dancing without caring who is watching.
experiment.whatToNotice: Notice if the loud, chaotic environment feels overwhelming or liberating.
experiment.commonTrap: Going with a large group of hesitant friends. Try going with one person who already loves it, or go alone.

name: Improv Comedy Class
shortDescription: Learn to perform unscripted scenes by actively listening and agreeing with your scene partners.
hook: A masterclass in letting go of control, being present, and failing joyfully.

experiment.smallestStep: Sign up for a one-off 2-hour 'intro to improv' drop-in class.
experiment.whatSuccessFeelsLike: Saying the first stupid thing that comes to mind and realizing nobody judges you.
experiment.whatToNotice: Notice how much energy it takes to 'yes, and' instead of blocking ideas.
experiment.commonTrap: Trying to be 'funny'. The best improv comes from reacting honestly, not making jokes.

name: Solo Fine Dining
shortDescription: Take yourself out to a high-end restaurant and eat a multi-course meal alone.
hook: Transform the anxiety of eating alone into a luxurious act of self-care and mindfulness.

experiment.smallestStep: Book a table for one at a highly-rated restaurant and leave your phone in your pocket.
experiment.whatSuccessFeelsLike: Feeling comfortable being perceived alone while savoring incredible flavors.
experiment.whatToNotice: Notice the urge to pull out your phone, and instead direct your attention to the ambiance and food.
experiment.commonTrap: Sitting at the bar staring at a screen. Get a table and fully engage with the experience.

name: Standup Open Mic
shortDescription: Write 3 minutes of jokes and perform them in front of a live, usually apathetic, audience.
hook: Conquer the ultimate fear of public speaking while turning your pain into punchlines.

experiment.smallestStep: Write out one funny story and sign up for a local open mic night.
experiment.whatSuccessFeelsLike: Getting off stage having survived, regardless of whether anyone laughed.
experiment.whatToNotice: Notice the adrenaline dump before and after holding the microphone.
experiment.commonTrap: Expecting to kill on your first night. Expect to bomb, it's a rite of passage.

name: Sensory Deprivation Tank
shortDescription: Float in pitch black, silent, body-temperature salt water for 60-90 minutes.
hook: Forced, absolute disconnection from the external world to explore your own mind.

experiment.smallestStep: Book a 60-minute float session at a local spa.
experiment.whatSuccessFeelsLike: Losing track of where your body ends and the water begins.
experiment.whatToNotice: Notice how your brain invents thoughts or sounds when deprived of external stimuli.
experiment.commonTrap: Getting out early because you feel restless. Push through the initial boredom.
